messages:
Maya: Quick chopshop — we need to lock scope for the next minor (0.3.1) today. Two customer asks vs two internal bugs. Options: bug-only patch vs mixed release with one enhancement. Need owners + release criteria by EOD.

Santiago: +1 for bug-first. The streaming token leak shows up in prod traces and spikes p99. Customer impact > perf improvement.

Li: I can own the leak fix. Root cause looks like prefix cache eviction when seq > 4096; I need to add a regression test and update KV cache eviction threshold. Est: 2 dev days + perf run.

Omar: Batching heuristic change would improve median latency and cost but has tail risk. If we include it, we need a perf window and an easy rollback (feature flag). Not comfortable adding it to the same release without canary metrics.

Claire: From CS: Acme is blocking on the leak, Nova is okay to wait for batching. Recommend ship bug patch now, schedule batching for 0.4.0. Offer Acme a temporary config workaround (limit seq length) in docs.

Maya: Proposed decision — ship bug-focused 0.3.1 (leak + small rate-limit retry UX). Defer batching to 0.4.0 unless we can prove safe in canary. Owners: Li (leak fix), Omar (release/rollout + flag), Santiago (monitoring & customer logs), Claire (customer comms). Release criteria below.

Maya: Release criteria (must all be true):
- unit/integration tests green
- leak regression test added and passing
- p99 latency within 2% of baseline in canary
- no new 5xx errors during 2h canary at 5% traffic
- rollback playbook validated

Santiago: I’ll add a canary dashboard slice for Acme/Nova and a quick eval suite (synthetic + sampled prod traces). Also granting Li access to Acme logs now.

Li: Thanks — opening PR in a bit. Patch summary in PR body and a small test harness.

Omar: I’ll add a feature flag `batching_heur_v2` (default off) and a runtime knob for seq-limit so Acme can be unblocked without code changes:

```yaml
service.runtime: 
  seq_limit: 4096
  batching_heur: v1
```

Omar: Will also wire a rollout flag for the canary: `deploy.canary_pct=5`.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started for 0.3.1 — canary-id=canary-171120, initial traffic 5%. CI status: running.

Claire: I’ll draft comms for Acme: workaround + expected timeline (48h). Also prepping FAQ for support team.

Maya: Agreement reached: bug-first. Action items: Li -> PR + tests (due +48h), Omar -> flags & rollback playbook (due EOD), Santiago -> dashboard + logs (inflight), Claire -> customer note (2h).

Li: PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/1425 — includes unit tests and a small perf script. Requesting review from Omar and Santiago.

Santiago: Review done, granted Li access to full Acme traces. Kicked off an eval run against canary.

deploy-bot: Canary finished stage 1: 3h running, no regressions detected on p50/p90, small p99 blip (-1.2%). Promoting to 100% at 12:00 UTC tomorrow unless objections.

Omar: I validated the rollback steps locally and added a smoke test to the deploy job: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/inference-runtime --to-revision={{prev}}` and a health-check script.

Claire: Customer note sent to Acme with workaround. They acknowledged and asked for ETA on full fix — I gave 48h.

Maya: Great run. Final reminder: log any follow-on enhancements as separate RFCs. Batching goes to 0.4.0 backlog with perf acceptance criteria. Reconvene after 100% promotion to confirm stable.

Santiago: Filing a short post-deploy eval doc (will link here).

Maya: Thanks team :thumbsup:
